title: Saving money at the Tivoli and deciding to go to Europe
summary: He describes the Tivoli job, pay versus tips, the Manti brothers, and reading about bands in Europe.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yes. I was, I saved so much money. I was young. I didn't know what to do with it. And Frank and his brother, they made me save some, they taught me to save. And my mother was sick at the time. And I had to send my salary home and keep my tips. Was that good? The tips, the salary was nothing next to the tips because the salary was $2.50 a day from 7 to 5 in the morning. That's $2.50. I was getting five pesos a day at that time. But we didn't make twice that much or much more than that on tips. Oh, yeah. So I'd send my salary to have my father with my mother and keep the tips. And that's how after two years, I felt myself becoming a man, although I wasn't. Not even here. But, you know, getting taller all the time and looking above everybody, especially in Mexico, the man's all short. And the Manti brothers, too, were short fellas. Didn't have five foot, something like that.
What was the name of that joint? Frank?

Tivoli. Well, and so I saved so much money. And I used to buy those different magazines in Mexico just to keep myself reading in English. Oh, yeah. And I read in some magazine about the bands that was in Europe. You see, in the Noble Sister, I think. Yeah. You record it. The Man Cook, the Man Cook, Wilman Cook was over, and Louie Mitchell was over there. And the old Pabr group of Breaktown was over. I heard a lot of those people back in, in, in, being in Europe. And how Europe was jumping. Yeah. So, I had saved so much money. I didn't know what to do with it. I said, I'm going to take a trip over there. And, uh, I had to have a passport. Well, I had so much trouble getting my birth certificate right. I almost had given up. My name wasn't right. You know, and everything else in it never got straight. Yeah. That's fast. But I finally did get my name straight. They wanted to make me G-W-D-Y, in which my name was G-O-U-D-I-E.
